import math

# Treasury Tax and Loan Account - Monthly Average Balance (1961) in millions of dollars
# From Treasury Bulletin data
treasury_balance = [3414, 3812, 3705, 2171, 3765, 3572, 3739, 4581, 4277, 5924, 4873, 3869]

# U.S. Unemployment Rate (1961) - from BLS/FRED
unemployment_rate = [6.6, 6.9, 6.9, 7.0, 7.1, 6.9, 7.0, 6.6, 6.7, 6.5, 6.1, 6.0]

# Calculate Pearson correlation coefficient
n = len(treasury_balance)

# Calculate means
mean_x = sum(treasury_balance) / n
mean_y = sum(unemployment_rate) / n

# Calculate Pearson correlation
numerator = sum((x - mean_x) * (y - mean_y) for x, y in zip(treasury_balance, unemployment_rate))
denominator_x = math.sqrt(sum((x - mean_x) ** 2 for x in treasury_balance))
denominator_y = math.sqrt(sum((y - mean_y) ** 2 for y in unemployment_rate))

r = numerator / (denominator_x * denominator_y)

print(f"Treasury Balance (millions): {treasury_balance}")
print(f"Unemployment Rate (%): {unemployment_rate}")
print(f"\nMean Treasury Balance: {mean_x:.2f}")
print(f"Mean Unemployment Rate: {mean_y:.4f}")
print(f"\nPearson correlation coefficient: {r:.4f}")
print(f"Rounded to 2 decimal places: {round(r, 2)}")
EOF
